blocks.text: Abdali next changes tactics by riding out with little ceremony so he can study the ground without revealing too much of his intention. He reconnoitres the approaches, measures heights and distances, and keeps the defenders guessing by shifting men forward and back instead of committing to an obvious assault.

Once darkness falls, he summons his commanders and reveals the engineering answer he has chosen. A forty feet high wall is ordered at the commanding point near the fort, and the work is pressed so quickly that the defenders cannot interfere before dawn.

By morning the Jats are astonished to find a new elevation towering over their position as if a mountain had risen overnight. Heavy weapons are mounted there, and the page turns the siege from stalemate into a carefully prepared bombardment that will soon break the balance.
